questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How to learn Czech quickly as an adult
A refugee child losing her first language
Life in Czechoslovakia during the Cold War
Why Canada accepts so many refugees each year
questions.why: They hear about Julie Sedivy, whose learning of English started to replace her native Czech.

questions.q: What was Julie's situation when her family arrived in Canada?
options: They spoke fluent English
They had lived in Canada before
They were political refugees who spoke no English
They came on holiday and decided to stay
questions.why: They arrived as political refugees with no English.

questions.q: How does Julie remember starting at an English-speaking school?
options: It was very frightening
It wasn't especially difficult for her
She refused to go
Her teachers spoke Czech to her
questions.why: She says her memory is that it was not particularly difficult or traumatic.

questions.q: Why wasn't Julie worried at school?
options: She had changed languages before and trusted it
Her older brothers and sisters helped her every day
She already spoke quite a lot of English
The school gave her a Czech translator
questions.why: She had been dunked into unfamiliar languages many times and had faith it would sort itself out.

questions.q: Which languages had Julie been exposed to before Canada?
options: Spanish and German
Russian and Polish
Only Czech
Italian and French
questions.why: Sam says she had been exposed to several languages including Italian and French.

questions.q: What sad result of losing Czech does Rob mention?
options: She couldn't get a good job in Canada
She had no friends at school for years
She lost the chance to speak Czech with her dad
She couldn't go back to the Czech Republic
questions.why: She forgot her native language, and with it the chance to speak Czech with her dad before he passed away.

questions.q: What does Julie believe about speaking several languages?
options: It makes you forget who you are
It is only useful for work
It confuses children
It gives you a greater sense of tolerance
questions.why: She believes speaking more languages means we gain a sense of tolerance.

questions.q: Why does Julie mention a Spanish-speaking American of Mexican background?
options: To show you can keep your language and belong
To show immigrants should stop speaking Spanish
To compare life in Mexico and Canada
To explain why she learned Spanish at school
questions.why: She says you can be of Mexican ancestry, speak Spanish, and be a full-fledged American.
